frames.narration: The crawler wants to store a fetched page under the row key com.cnn.www/index.html. It does not know which tablet server holds that row. It reads a Chubby file that points to the root tablet, then the METADATA tablets, to find the tablet whose row range contains the key. It remembers the answer for next time.

The client sends the write straight to the tablet server. The master is not involved, which is why it stays lightly loaded. The server checks that the write is well formed and that the sender is allowed to write.
The server first appends the change to its commit log in GFS, with group commit for many small writes. Only a change that is in the log counts as safe.
Then the change goes into the memtable, a sorted buffer in memory, and the client gets its answer. The write cost one sequential log append and one memory update, not a random disk write.

A read for the same row is served from a merged view of the memtable and the SSTables, newest first. A Bloom filter on each SSTable says whether the row might be inside, so files that cannot hold it are skipped without a disk read.

When the memtable reaches its size threshold it is frozen and written to GFS as a new immutable SSTable, which is a minor compaction. The log up to that point is no longer needed for recovery. Later, compactions merge SSTables and a major compaction drops deleted data.

The tablet server crashes with new writes in its memtable. The master sees that the server lost its Chubby lock and gives its tablets to other servers. The new server reads the tablet's metadata, loads the SSTable indexes and replays the commit log from the redo point, so the memtable comes back with every acknowledged write.
